definitions.E: L-n*d, the total degree excess of nonpivot variables above d
definitions.e_y: degree excess of nonpivot variable y, so deg(y)=d+e_y and sum e_y=E
definitions.s_y: number of pivot-parent clauses omitting y; exactly s_y=t_y-e_y
definitions.Omax_T: max sum_y f_p_q(s_y) subject to 0<=s_y<=min(c,d) and sum_y s_y=T

statement: For every unit-free canonical ordinary CNF state and every actual selected minimum-degree pivot of degree d with split p+q=d, set E=L-n*d. For a feasible retained literal mass R0, total omission count among pivot parents is exactly T=R0-E. Thus total pair-support mass is at least Smin(R0)=r*pq-Omax(R0-E). If D distinct non-tautological resolvents exist and h of them coincide with retained clauses, then K=c+D-h global raw clauses must satisfy R0+max(0,Smin-(pq-D)r)-h*r<=Wmax_r(K), K<=3^r. Therefore raw_units is at most the maximum 1+K+Wmax_r(K) over all feasible integer R0,D,h. This strictly generalizes the regular L=n*d theorem, which is the E=0 case.
proof: The selected pivot has degree exactly d. Every other live variable has degree at least d because d is the minimum. Write deg(y)=d+e_y with e_y>=0. Summing degrees gives sum_y e_y=L-n*d=E.

For a nonpivot variable y, let t_y be its retained incidence. Its incidence among the d pivot-parent clauses is d+e_y-t_y. Therefore its omission count among those d parents is s_y=d-(d+e_y-t_y)=t_y-e_y>=0.
Summing over nonpivot variables gives sum_y s_y=R0-E. Also s_y<=c because t_y<=c, and s_y<=d because there are only d pivot parents.

If a_y of the p positive parents and b_y of the q negative parents omit y, then a_y+b_y=s_y and exactly a_y*b_y cross-polarity parent pairs omit y. Hence omitted pair-variable incidences are at most Omax(R0-E), and total pair-support mass is at least Smin=r*pq-Omax(R0-E).

Choose one parent pair for each of D distinct non-tautological resolvents. Removing the other pq-D pairs discards at most (pq-D)r support mass, so representative resolvent widths total at least max(0,Smin-(pq-D)r).

The c retained clauses have total width R0. If h distinct resolvents coincide with retained clauses, retained-plus-resolvent width double-counts at most h*r. Thus K=c+D-h distinct raw clauses have literal mass at least R0+representative_width_lower-h*r.
K distinct signed non-tautological clauses over r variables have total width at most Wmax_r(K), and K<=3^r. Therefore only the stated integer triples are feasible.

At a unit-free stage 2c<=R0, every pivot-parent clause has at least one tail literal so R0<=L-2d, and trivially R0<=c*r. Also R0>=E because sum omissions R0-E is nonnegative. Scanning this finite interval and all D,h yields a deterministic exact resource ceiling.
No runtime decision changes: this theorem is invoked only to certify resource availability of the already frozen exact elimination.
